thread:
Josh: Quick question about the generation API contract — saw a small change in my PR that might affect stop+max_tokens behavior, want a quick sanity check.

Ellie: what's the change?

Josh: I updated internal logic to run token-limit check before stop-match to avoid producing too-long outputs in bursty batching. Concern is backward compatibility for customers relying on stop sequences to be honored even if stop lives past max_tokens. Example request I pasted in the PR: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"rwd-model-x\",
  \"prompt\": \"Hello\",
  \"max_tokens\": 2,
  \"stop\": [\" world\"],
  \"temperature\": 0.0,
  \"top_p\": 0.0,
  \"logprobs\": 5
}
```
Does our contract say stop should be checked on decoded string and can cause early termination even if it would have required more tokens than max_tokens?

Kevin: current runtime historically does: emit token -> append decoded text buffer -> check stop sequences against buffer -> if matched, stop and trim stop from output. We also stop if emitted token count reaches max_tokens. So stop can only trigger if decoded prefix contains stop before hitting max_tokens. If stop only matches across token boundary and you would have needed to emit the token that completes the stop but that token is the one that would exceed max_tokens, then you won't emit it.

Amanda: Important: external contract should be "stop matching runs on decoded output; only emitted tokens count toward max_tokens". That implies we don't attempt to emit extra tokens to complete a stop. If users set max_tokens too low, stop may never match. We should document that.

Samir: Small note on temperature/top_p: using temperature=0.0 and top_p=0.0 is ambiguous. Some libs treat top_p=0 as disable, others treat 0 as degenerate. We shouldn't accept both zero without warning. We had a bug where top_p==0 made sampling return uniform random because of a divide-by-zero fallback. Recommend rejecting top_p <= 0 or normalizing 0->1.0 in the server.

Ellie: Also behavior for logprobs: if max_tokens==0 or stop matches immediately so no tokens emitted, do we return choices with an empty text and logprobs:null or an choice object with logprobs empty arrays? Current client expectations vary.

Josh: Right now the hosted API returns: choices: [{text:'', logprobs: null}] and usage.total_tokens=0. But our unit tests are flaky because older SDKs expect logprobs to be an object with arrays (empty) not null. Backcompat risk.

Amanda: Action items: add a compatibility note in the PR describing exact contract, add tests for: (1) stop longer than max_tokens, (2) stop crossing token boundaries, (3) logprobs requested with zero emitted tokens. @Samir can you add the validation for top_p/temperature? @Kevin can you confirm decoder order and add explicit comment in code? I can add the tests in generation_test.py if you want.

Samir: Yep I'll add a validation warning and a unit test for invalid top_p values. I propose server returns 400 if top_p<=0 or if temperature<0, with a migration note. Or alternatively coerce top_p==0 -> 1.0 but that might be surprising. Leaning toward 400 + helpful message.

Kevin: I'll add code comment and one unit test for stop detection on decoded text. Quick note: we should ensure batching doesn't merge partial buffers across requests (that caused an earlier bug). I verified current KV-cache per-request isolation.

Ellie: Also recommend we explicitly state in docs: "Stops are matched against decoded UTF-8 text after each emitted token; stop contents are removed from the returned text and are not counted toward max_tokens. If a stop requires emitting a token that would exceed max_tokens, the stop will not be satisfied." Short and precise.

Amanda: @Josh PTAL at PR description update. I'll create a small compatibility entry for the changelog and a test matrix.

aria-bot: Canary started for branch sampling-params-fix to eng-ml-dedicated (5% traffic) :rocket:

Josh: Perfect. One more edge case: when logprobs is requested but we return early due to stop that contains characters that were produced as part of the same token, do we still provide token-level logprobs for that token? i.e., logprobs correspond to emitted tokens only, not to the trimmed stop substring. That seems logical but callout for clients expecting logprobs mapping to final text positions.

Kevin: Confirmed — logprobs map to emitted tokens. If stop trimming removes chars from tail, token logprobs remain tied to tokens. We'll add a doc note explaining that mapping and an example.

Samir: I'll include a tiny migration FAQ: "If you depend on stop being matched even when max_tokens would be exceeded, increase max_tokens or post-process on client side."

Ellie: Sounds like a plan. Can we fold this into the release notes for the next SDK bump? Add a short entry under "Generation".

Amanda: I'll handle release-note bullet and add the tests in the PR. Kevin/Samir please ping when your commits are up. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
